# demo


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

`demo` renders ordinary FastHTML markup in an isolated document with the
registry’s current styles, behaviors, and browser helpers from
`reg.hdrs()`, matching a served app. Previews work in notebooks and
generated docs without an asset server.

``` python
from answerui.registry import hypelt
from fastcore.test import *
from fasthtml.common import P, Details, Summary
from answerui.controls import Btn
from answerui.overlays import Dropdown
```

## Rendering previews

Each preview document includes a stylesheet, behavior script, browser
helpers, the icon `spritesheet`, and htmx. FastHTML’s `def_hdrs` returns
the default app headers: charset and viewport meta tags, htmx 2, and
FastHTML’s helper script. `def_hdrs(htmx4=True)` returns htmx 4 instead
with an `htmx-config` meta tag setting `metaCharacter` to `-`, matching
`fast_app(htmx4=True)`. `demo_html` passes `surreal=False` to omit
Surreal.

htmx comes before the behavior script in `<head>` because the behavior
script registers with htmx. Both load before the page body, which
includes `spritesheet`. Pass `css` to substitute a custom stylesheet
without changing the registry, or `registry` to use another registry’s
stylesheet, behavior script, and browser helpers instead of `reg`.

`demo_html` sets inline `min-block-size: auto` on `body` to override any
full-viewport minimum height rule from the stylesheet. Without that
override, an auto-resizing iframe would grow without end.

When FastHTML serves a page, it renames `get`, `post`, `put`, `delete`,
`patch`, and `link` to `hx-get`, `hx-post`, `hx-put`, `hx-delete`,
`hx-patch`, and `href`, turning each value into a URL. In a preview,
`demo_html` renames those same attributes while keeping each path
unchanged. Pass `routes` as a dict mapping `'METHOD path'` keys such as
`'GET /saved'` to canned FastHTML responses. On a matching
`htmx:beforeRequest` event, an inline script cancels the network request
and swaps the canned markup into the target. It uses the element’s
inherited `hx-swap` style, defaulting to `innerHTML`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### demo_html

``` python
def demo_html(
    *fts, # Markup to render
    registry:answerui.registry.Registry=Registry(21 rules, 21 elements), # Registry providing styles, behaviors, and browser helpers
    css:NoneType=None, # Custom CSS string; None uses the styles from registry.hdrs()
    htmx4:bool=False, # Use htmx 4 with FastHTML's config, as `fast_app(htmx4=True)` does, instead of htmx 2
    routes:NoneType=None, # Canned htmx responses as {'METHOD path': markup}
):
```

*A standalone HTML document containing markup, CSS, behaviors, browser
helpers, icon spritesheet, and FastHTML’s default headers*

In notebooks, `demo` renders the preview inside an iframe. That isolates
the preview from the host notebook’s CSS, such as Solveit’s styles, in
both directions. The iframe’s `srcdoc` attribute holds the complete
document from `demo_html`. Unless you pass `height`, an inline
`ResizeObserver` script resizes the iframe to fit its content. Pass
`width` to preview a narrow viewport. A replay button above the iframe
reloads `srcdoc` to restart dynamic components such as a self-dismissing
notice.

Because the iframe contains the full stylesheet and scripts, storing its
HTML in every notebook output would bloat the file. `demo` returns a
`Preview` object with two representations: the iframe as `text/html` for
live display, and the markup alone as `text/markdown` for saved
notebooks and language models.


*A rendered preview: the iframe as HTML for live display, and the markup
as Markdown for saved notebooks and models*

A preview does not require a registered component. Here `css=''`
replaces the registry’s stylesheet with an empty one, showing a native
element exactly as the browser draws it:

``` python
demo(Details(Summary('More information'), P('This disclosure is a native details element.')), css='')
```

``` html
<details><summary>More information</summary>  <p>This disclosure is a native details element.</p>
</details>
```

Let’s recreate the notice from the earlier notebooks with one `hypelt`
call that registers its styles and behaviors together. Clicking its
`dismiss` button removes the notice. With `autodismiss` set, the `init`
handler removes the notice after that many milliseconds (4000 by
default) once htmx loads it.

``` python
notice_css = r"""
display: block;
padding: .75rem 1rem;
background: #f4f4f6;
border: 1px solid #ccc;
border-radius: 8px;
"""
NoticeBox = hypelt('NoticeBox', css=notice_css, layer='components', on={
    ('& [dismiss]', 'click'): r"el.closest('notice-box').remove()",
    ('&[autodismiss]', 'init'): r"await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, +el.getAttribute('autodismiss') || 4000)); el.remove()"},
    doc='A dismissible notice.')
```

Click Dismiss, then click the replay button to restore the notice:

``` python
demo(NoticeBox('Changes saved. ', Button('Dismiss', type='button', dismiss=True)))
```

``` html
<notice-box>Changes saved. <button type="button" dismiss>Dismiss</button></notice-box>
```

`_repr_mimebundle_` returns both representations with
`{'nbdev': {'strip': ['text/html']}}` metadata. `nbdev-clean` uses that
metadata to strip the iframe HTML from saved notebook outputs and keep
the Markdown:

``` python
bundle, meta = demo(NoticeBox('Changes saved.'))._repr_mimebundle_()
meta
```

    {'nbdev': {'strip': ['text/html']}}

This notice disappears after four seconds:

``` python
demo(NoticeBox('This notice disappears after four seconds.', autodismiss=4000), height='4rem')
```

``` html
<notice-box autodismiss="4000">This notice disappears after four seconds.</notice-box>
```

Here the Save button requests `/saved`. The canned response returns a
`NoticeBox` and a `Dropdown` (a trigger and a panel). The routes script
swaps the complete fragment into place as a served route would. Click
Save, open Next action, then click the replay button to reset the
preview.

``` python
demo(Button('Save', type='button', get='/saved', hx_swap='outerHTML'),
    routes={'GET /saved': (NoticeBox('Saved.'), Dropdown('Next action', Btn('Keep'), Btn('Remove')))})
```

``` html
<button type="button" hx-swap="outerHTML" hx-get="/saved">Save</button>
```

Passing `htmx4=True` includes the same htmx 4 headers and FastHTML
config as `fast_app(htmx4=True)`. The behavior script runs `init`
handlers through `htmx.onLoad`, which under that config listens for htmx
4’s `htmx-after-process` event on newly arrived content. The notice’s
timer still starts:

``` python
demo(NoticeBox('This notice disappears after four seconds under htmx 4.', autodismiss=4000), htmx4=True, height='4rem')
```

``` html
<notice-box autodismiss="4000">This notice disappears after four seconds under htmx 4.</notice-box>
```

Here we pass a candidate stylesheet via `css` that replaces the notice’s
grey background with pale yellow. The registered behaviors still apply.

``` python
candidate_css = NoticeBox.rules['base'].compiled_css.replace('#f4f4f6', '#fff4cc')
demo(NoticeBox('Trying a warmer surface. ', Button('Dismiss', type='button', dismiss=True)), css=candidate_css)
```

``` html
<notice-box>Trying a warmer surface. <button type="button" dismiss>Dismiss</button></notice-box>
```

To register an application override for all later previews and
application pages, call `NoticeBox.rule`. It adds CSS to the `app` layer
without changing the notice’s base definition or behaviors:

``` python
NoticeBox.rule('corners', 'border-radius: 1rem;', doc='Rounder notice corners.')
demo(NoticeBox('The current stylesheet includes the application override.'))
```

``` html
<notice-box>The current stylesheet includes the application override.</notice-box>
```

## Reusable examples

Use the `example` decorator to attach a no-argument markup function to a
hyperelement as `NoticeBox.example`. Calling `NoticeBox.demo()` renders
that markup with the hyperelement’s registry.

Attaching another example replaces the previous one. To show multiple
variants, return them together from one function.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Hyperelement.demo

``` python
def demo(
    *, css:NoneType=None, # Custom CSS string; None uses the styles from registry.hdrs()
    height:NoneType=None, # Fixed iframe height (e.g. '10rem') for top-layer content ResizeObserver cannot measure; None resizes to content
    width:NoneType=None, # Fixed iframe width, e.g. '24rem', to preview a narrow viewport; None fills the cell
    htmx4:bool=False, # Use htmx 4 with FastHTML's config, as `fast_app(htmx4=True)` does, instead of htmx 2
    routes:NoneType=None, # Canned htmx responses as {'METHOD path': markup}
):
```

*Render this hyperelement’s example with its registry’s current styles
and behaviors*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### example

``` python
def example(
    h
):
```

*Decorator that stores a no-argument markup function as `h.example`, for
`h.demo()` to render*

``` python
@example(NoticeBox)
def notice_example():
    return Div(NoticeBox('Changes saved. ', Button('Dismiss', type='button', dismiss=True)),
        NoticeBox('This notice stays visible.'), style='display:grid;gap:1rem')
```

The example itself is ordinary markup:

``` python
to_xml(NoticeBox.example())
```

    '<div style="display:grid;gap:1rem">\n<notice-box>Changes saved. <button type="button" dismiss>Dismiss</button></notice-box><notice-box>This notice stays visible.</notice-box></div>\n'

`NoticeBox.demo()` renders it with the current styles and behaviors:

``` python
NoticeBox.demo()
```

``` html
<div style="display:grid;gap:1rem">
<notice-box>Changes saved. <button type="button" dismiss>Dismiss</button></notice-box><notice-box>This notice stays visible.</notice-box></div>
```

`NoticeBox.example()` returns fresh FastHTML markup that can be
inspected or reused in a larger composition. `NoticeBox.demo()` accepts
`demo`’s options, such as `height` and `css`. Each call to
`NoticeBox.demo()` builds a new document from the current example,
styles, and behaviors. Clicking the replay button instead restarts
interactions by reloading the existing `srcdoc` in the iframe without
running Python.

Because each shipped component’s notebook exports its `@example`
function, importing the component’s module attaches the example without
rendering anything.

Registering `corners` again replaces the earlier rule in place. The next
`NoticeBox.demo()` builds its document with the square corners:

``` python
NoticeBox.rule('corners', 'border-radius: 0;', doc='Square notice corners.')
NoticeBox.demo()
```

``` html
<div style="display:grid;gap:1rem">
<notice-box>Changes saved. <button type="button" dismiss>Dismiss</button></notice-box><notice-box>This notice stays visible.</notice-box></div>
```

Calling `hypelt` again with the same name updates the existing
`NoticeBox` in place, keeping its example:

``` python
NoticeBox = hypelt('NoticeBox', css=notice_css, layer='components', doc='A persistent notice.')
test_is(NoticeBox.example, notice_example)
NoticeBox.demo()
```

``` html
<div style="display:grid;gap:1rem">
<notice-box>Changes saved. <button type="button" dismiss>Dismiss</button></notice-box><notice-box>This notice stays visible.</notice-box></div>
```
